newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures erode gains late, end mixed.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures erode gains late, end mixed.

text.p: U.S. interest rate futures eroded during the final hour, with the long end erasing small midmorning gains and slipping to equally small daily losses.
U.S. Treasury bond futures began pulling back after results of the 10-year T-note auction were announced.
The $10 billion in 10-year notes sold at an average yield of 6.273 percent with a one-basis-point tail, or the spread between average and high yields and an indication of demand.
Bid/cover ratio, or amount of bids received against those accepted, was 2.41. Non-competitive bids, or those from small investors and which do not include a yield, were $306 million.
Although some traders called the results in-line with most estimates, they said the market had built up some expectations of even stronger demand and also was technically vulnerable.
"It did go well. It's right in line," said one floor broker. "But they did talk it up so much...and if we go below the low at 113-17/32, it could be a dark day down here."
During the last hour, December T-bonds did probe below 113-17/32 and set the session's price trough at 113-16/32.
But the move lower encountered sizable dealer buying in brisk late turnover and as the market mulled Thursday's final leg of the quarterly refunding, brokers said.
Treasury will sell $10.0 billion in 30-year bonds on Thursday.
"It was like, 'Katie, bar the door,'" said a T-bond futures floor broker of the day's price action. "It was all over the place."

He said the day's volume in the T-bond pit likely will prove high and said much trade occurred during the last couple hours of the session. "Net-net, the market's in good shape, (although) a little bit overbought," he added of the technical picture. "We're only down four ticks. The market's just digesting its huge gains."

Futures slipped early on long liquidation after the U.S. presidential and Congressional races ended much as expected. Nearby T-bonds firmed again near midday after holding support near 113-16/32, with dealer buying spooking locals into covering shorts, before the contract drifted at higher levels.
"It always makes highs slower than lows - the escalator up and the elevator shaft down," quipped another floor broker.

Dec T-bonds ended down 5/32 at 113-20/32, 10-year notes lost 1/32 to 110-00, muni-bonds fell 11/32 to 116-08/32, March T-bills rose one bp to 94.96, and March Eurodollars ended unchanged at 94.46. -Derivatives Desk(312)408-8750/E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
